title: A Spire for the Salt
premise: Orsen Villalobos keeps the ledgers of the Saltspire Guild, a smuggling ring that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When the usurper King Aldric declares a hunt for anyone carrying the gift, Orsen's careful invisibility shatters: her own ledgers are the map the crown needs to find every gifted soul in the free cities. Torn between loyalty to the guildmaster who saved her and the truth that he has been selling the hunted to the crown, she must find the Door of Brine—the last way out of a country that officially no longer exists. In the end, she burns the ledgers, exposes the guildmaster to those he betrayed, and holds the Door open long enough for others to pass through, staying behind as its keeper rather than escaping herself.
about_author: Coral Coldharbour grew up in a fishing town whose harbor silted over before she was born, and she has spent her life writing about places that outlive their own maps. She lives near tidal flats, where she collects sea glass and insists the tide keeps better records than any government.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Orsen Villalobos audits the Saltspire Guild's accounts: a jarred thunderclap sold to a grieving widow, three days of borrowed youth traded for a fisherman's luck. Through her POV we learn she is a runaway apprentice hiding a small gift of her own—she can read what objects remember. Emotional beat: wary contentment built on concealment.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane Dhal assigns Orsen to catalog a new acquisition: a door-shaped slab of salt that hums when she touches it. Her gift shows her a country that vanished from all maps two generations ago. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: fascination edged with dread—the first hint her past will not stay buried.

chapters.title: A Proclamation Nailed to Every Door
chapters.summary: Crown criers announce King Aldric's Edict of Cleansing: all bearers of the gift must register or be hunted. The free cities' guilds scramble. POV shifts to Sergeant Ilsa Merrin, a reluctant hunter who believes order is mercy. Emotional beat: the safe world tilting; Orsen realizes her ledgers are evidence.

chapters.title: What the Books Would Confess
chapters.summary: Orsen secretly begins altering entries to hide gifted clients, discovering her gift lets her rewrite an object's memory at a cost—each edit erases something from her own. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve; she chooses others' safety over her own wholeness.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Names
chapters.summary: A masked client buys passage and pays with true names of the gifted—a betrayal list. Orsen recognizes the handwriting as Corvane's. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: cold shock; the man who sheltered her may be selling his people.

chapters.title: Sergeant Merrin's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Isla Merrin interrogates a registered hedge-witch and finds the arithmetic of mercy failing: registration feeds pyres, not protection. POV Isla. Emotional beat: doubt cracking duty; she pockets a name instead of reporting it.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Orsen tests the salt door at low tide and opens it a crack onto a shore under a sun that isn't theirs—the lost country of Vael still exists behind the brine. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: awe and terror; escape is real, but so is whatever guards it.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Orsen's memory-reading of an old guild token: how Corvane bought her off the road at fourteen, and what he asked in return—her gift, quietly, forever. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: grief reframing gratitude as debt and leash.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Convene
chapters.summary: Guild delegates meet in smuggler's parliament to decide: flee, fight, or bargain. Corvane argues for bargaining; a young fire-gifted delegate named Sefa argues for the Door. POV Sefa. Emotional beat: fractious hope; factions harden into futures.

chapters.title: A Hunt in the Warrens
chapters.summary: Isla's unit sweeps the undercity; Orsen guides a family of gifted through routes only ledger-keepers know. The two women nearly meet across a locked gate. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: breathless chase; enemies glimpsed as mirrors.

chapters.title: The Price of One Edit Too Many
chapters.summary: Orsen rewrites the guild's master ledger wholesale to blind the crown's auditors—and loses her memory of her mother's face. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: devastating cost made concrete; survival priced in selfhood.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Tidehouse
chapters.summary: Corvane meets the crown's envoy secretly; Orsen shadows him and hears him offer the Door itself in exchange for the guild's charter. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; love curdles into clarity.

chapters.title: Sefa's Fire
chapters.summary: Sefa discovers Corvane's list includes her own name and nearly burns the guildhall down; Orsen talks her down by confessing everything—the ledgers, the edits, the Door. POV Sefa. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into alliance; truth as the price of loyalty kept.

chapters.title: Isla Deserts
chapters.summary: Ordered to burn a registered village that resisted, Isla refuses, frees its people, and becomes hunted herself—carrying the very list she once helped enforce. POV Isla. Emotional beat: fall from grace into conscience; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Three Thieves of a Country
chapters.summary: Orsen, Sefa, and Isla converge at the Tidehouse to steal the salt door before the crown's wagons arrive. A heist through fog and gunpowder-smell. Rotating POV. Emotional beat: exhilaration and trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes His Hand
chapters.summary: Corvane catches them mid-theft; he reveals the Door only opens for a keeper who gives it a true name freely given—and he intends that name to be Orsen's, binding her to the guild forever. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: trap within trap; the ultimate claim on her loyalty.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Army Reaches the Shallows
chapters.summary: Aldric's vanguard arrives; the free cities burn their own harbors to slow him. Refugees flood toward rumor of a door. Wide-lens chapter, mostly Isla's POV organizing the desperate. Emotional beat: apocalyptic urgency; time runs out like a tide.

chapters.title: Ledgers in the Fire
chapters.summary: Orsen burns the guild's books publicly, freeing every hidden name—including her own—so no one can be found or owned by paper again. Corvane watches his empire become ash. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: liberation through destruction; truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Door of Brine
chapters.summary: At the drowned quay, Orsen offers her full true name—not to Corvane but to the Door itself—and it opens wide onto Vael's living shore. The first refugees cross as crown cavalry charges. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: sacrifice crystallizing; she chooses the threshold over the far side.

chapters.title: What Corvane Carried
chapters.summary: Corvane, offered passage, instead stays to hold the rearguard against the cavalry—his final payment on a debt older than Orsen. POV Corvane. Emotional beat: redemption too late to be simple, real enough to matter.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Threshold
chapters.summary: The army breaks against the Door's closing tide; Isla and Sefa lead the last column through while Orsen remains as keeper, the one soul both countries agree not to hunt. POV Isla watching from the far shore. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph; justice kept alive outside every law.

chapters.title: A Spire for the Salt
chapters.summary: Epilogue: on Vael's shore, refugees raise a spire of white stone over the sealed Door, and Orsen—older, half-erased, whole in her own accounting—begins a new ledger recording not debts but gifts freely given. POV Orsen. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; the price paid, the meaning kept.
